state_model.claim_rule: TOKEN_VAZIO, PENDING and FAIL never authorize an external claim.
state_model.evidence_rule: A claim may only be promoted inside the scope demonstrated by same-commit or explicitly historical evidence.

gaps.title: ARM64 ELF identity inside the current APK
evidence: CI validates structural ARM64 routes but does not prove current ELF identity inside an installed APK
gaps.next_action: Generate one current-commit APK containing the ARM64 ELF, extract it independently and compare cryptographic identity.

closure.condition: The ARM64 ELF embedded in the current APK is independently extracted and hash-identical to the current build artifact.

gaps.title: Physical Android install, launch and runtime receipt for the current artifact
evidence: PR and main CI are green; device runtime remains outside those gates
gaps.next_action: Install the same current APK on an authorized Android device, launch/dlopen it and record logcat/exit with artifact hashes.

closure.condition: Same-commit APK is installed and launched on an authorized device with a bounded runtime receipt and no unaccounted crash.
required_gates: adb install or equivalent authorized install

gaps.title: Repository licensing and third-party redistribution decision
gaps.next_action: Human owner selects the intended licensing model after authorship and third-party compatibility review; then add the corresponding root license and notices.

closure.condition: A human-authorized license decision is recorded and repository/third-party terms are made internally consistent.
required_artifacts: root license text or explicit proprietary terms
required_gates: GitHub license detection or explicit documented exception

gaps.title: Verified private vulnerability reporting channel
provenance: GitHub private vulnerability reporting setting is not readable by the current integration
evidence: Security policy is versioned; private reporting enablement remains unverified
gaps.next_action: Enable or verify GitHub private vulnerability reporting and record a non-sensitive administrative receipt.

closure.condition: A private vulnerability intake path is demonstrably available and its handling workflow is documented.
required_artifacts: private reporting setting receipt or approved private contact mechanism

gaps.title: Release-grade SBOM and third-party license inventory
provenance: release V1.0.0 has no attached assets
gaps.next_action: Generate a deterministic machine-readable SBOM plus third-party notices for a named release artifact and bind both to its commit/hash.

closure.condition: Named release artifact has reproducible SBOM, third-party inventory and provenance bound to the same commit.

gaps.title: Internal custody ledger cross-environment closure and issue reconciliation
evidence: Schema and CI ledger checks exist; issue remains open and Termux execution is still a named acceptance item
gaps.next_action: Run the current ledger writer/verifier on Termux, preserve the receipt, reconcile each issue #121 checkbox and close only if all acceptance conditions are evidenced.

closure.condition: Current writer/verifier passes both Linux CI and Termux with tamper-negative tests, and issue #121 is reconciled against receipts.

gaps.title: Real cryptographic authority signatures for federated receipts
evidence: Issue #134 explicitly records ED25519 as TOKEN_VAZIO_PLACEHOLDER
gaps.next_action: Replace the placeholder with a verifiable signing contract or explicitly remove signature claims from the federated protocol.

closure.condition: Federated receipt signatures are cryptographically verifiable with documented key lifecycle, or signature claims are removed from the contract.

gaps.title: Cross-repository physical receipts and federated reconciliation
evidence: 11/11 local authority artifacts are reconciled, but federated runtime/receipts remain unverified
gaps.next_action: Produce at least one real authority submission -> review -> receipt -> aggregate chain across repositories with immutable identities.

closure.condition: A cross-repo receipt chain binds repository, commit, artifact, authority and aggregate, and an independent verifier accepts it while rejecting tampering.

gaps.title: Deterministic cross_repo_bridge_v1 for RafGitTools and FlorisBoard
evidence: Issue #298 defines node/edge contract but adapter/schema/view are not yet closed
gaps.next_action: Implement artifact_ref ingestion, typed nodes/edges, deterministic view and tests while excluding typed IME content by default.

closure.condition: Schema + adapter + deterministic cross_repo_bridge_v1 reconstruct only from source manifests/receipts and preserve claim boundaries.

gaps.title: Executable privacy boundary for FlorisBoard/IME integration
evidence: Issue #298 states typed content is out of scope by default; executable enforcement is not yet evidenced
gaps.next_action: Encode and test an allowlist of metadata fields for the bridge so typed text/content cannot enter the derived graph by default.

closure.condition: Bridge fixtures prove typed content is rejected or excluded by default and only approved metadata is ingested.

gaps.title: Current reproducible release with attached artifacts and checksums
provenance: GitHub release V1.0.0 observed as prerelease dated 2026-06-14 with zero attached assets
gaps.next_action: Create a release candidate from a current green commit with immutable artifact manifest, checksums, provenance and explicit limitations.

closure.condition: A current release candidate contains named downloadable artifacts, checksums, provenance and reproducible build instructions.

gaps.title: Commercial support, maintenance and lifecycle decision
gaps.next_action: Choose supported release channels, maintenance window, security response expectations and whether any SLA is offered; do not imply one before approval.

closure.condition: Human-approved support/lifecycle policy defines supported channels, maintenance semantics and non-promissory or contractual response terms.

gaps.title: Independent user, buyer or research validation
gaps.next_action: Obtain independent install/reproduction or a bounded pilot and preserve the external receipt without converting interest into efficacy claims.

closure.condition: At least one independent party reproduces a declared workflow or pilot under documented conditions and limitations.

gaps.title: External compliance/security assessment when certification is claimed
gaps.next_action: Only if a certification/conformity claim becomes a business requirement, define scope and engage a competent independent assessor; until then use alignment language only.

closure.condition: Any external conformity claim is supported by scope-specific independent assessment or certification evidence.

gaps.title: Independent technical reproduction of core claims
evidence: Internal CI proves named gates; independent reproduction is not implied
gaps.next_action: Publish a bounded reproduction protocol and have an independent environment rerun core compiler/provenance/runtime gates.

closure.condition: Independent execution reproduces the selected claim set from documented inputs and records both positive and negative results.

gaps.title: Reconcile high-risk historical completion claims with current evidence
evidence: The root decision supplement classifies the document HIGH/review-required rather than current evidence
gaps.next_action: Map each quantitative/production claim to current receipt, historical receipt or TOKEN_VAZIO and move/archive only through a dedicated review PR.

closure.condition: Every strong historical claim has an evidence state and the document is clearly separated from current operational truth.

gaps.title: Observable branch protection and merge-control policy
provenance: AGENTS.md requires non-protected branch work by policy
GitHub branch protection endpoint returned inaccessible to current integration
gaps.next_action: Verify repository rulesets/branch protection in GitHub settings and record only non-sensitive policy facts such as required checks and review rules.

closure.condition: Main branch merge controls are observable and consistent with the repository's human-authorization and required-check policy.

edges.rationale: Runtime claim for the ARM64 path requires identity of the ARM64 artifact inside the tested APK.
Third-party release must not silently invent redistribution rights.
Release-grade distribution requires component and third-party provenance.
A support lifecycle needs an explicit vulnerability intake path before security expectations are offered.
Commercial support packaging depends on the owner's licensing/distribution model.
Federated receipts need the local custody event model to be closed across execution environments.
The current federated contract references signatures; real aggregate claims require a verifiable signature path or removal of that claim.
FlorisBoard integration must enforce the stated default exclusion of typed content.
A deterministic bridge provides a consumption surface for real cross-repo receipts without replacing source authority.
External evaluators need a bounded, downloadable, identified artifact.
Claims about Android utility require at least one current physical runtime path before commercial validation is meaningful.
Independent reproduction needs immutable inputs and build instructions.
A formal external assessment scope should include legal/IP obligations if commercial distribution is in scope.
Security/compliance assessment benefits from an operational vulnerability intake process.
Removing ambiguity between historical and current claims reduces reproduction drift.
Observable merge controls reduce release provenance risk.
Commercial reuse terms remain ambiguous until the owner makes the licensing decision.
